recommendation: Keep the source fix. Do not publish a separate FHIR-46453 decision from this default Applied/Published seed run, but this change should satisfy its source correction if that issue is later audited; regression-test follow-up can be handled under FHIR-46453 if desired.
issue_request: FHIR-8889 was Published/Persuasive and asked that the dateTime validation regex require a timezone/UTC offset whenever hours and minutes are supplied, matching the datatype SHALL statement.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 7195. Git-svn commit 02da8332d164281d0bbbd3ac45617afb7334c1da applied #8889 by changing the old datatype narrative regex so the offset branch was no longer optional when time was present.
additional_context: Later R5 regex work, especially FHIR-34355, changed the dateTime regex and reintroduced the ability to match a full dateTime without an offset. Published FHIR-38735 and Applied FHIR-52878 later narrowed offsets back to the time branch, and Resolved-change-required FHIR-46453 explicitly identified the remaining full-time-without-offset behavior as a regression of FHIR-8889. The current datatype prose still says a UTC offset SHALL be populated when hours and minutes are specified.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/primitives.xml to require Z or a signed UTC offset inside the dateTime time branch, while preserving the later correction that date-only and partial-date values do not carry offsets. No generated artifacts were edited.
source_changes: source/datatypes/primitives.xml: changed the dateTime regex so YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.fraction] must be followed by Z or a signed UTC offset, while year/year-month/date-only values remain valid without offsets.
